9	/-!
10	# The invariants as a limit **over the base**: closing the category mismatch
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean` proved that the invariant subring is the limit of a group
13	action — in `CommRingCat`, with no base ring. Its §4 then flagged, as the third of three open
14	items, that this is **the wrong category** for the consumer:
15	
16	> **The category.** `SymPowColimit`'s affine statement is over `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`; everything here
17	> is over `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`. No declaration bridges them, so nothing in that file can consume
18	> anything in this one.
19	
20	That item is closed here, and closed by *restating rather than bridging* — which turned out
21	to be the cheaper route. Rather than transporting the `CommRingCat` limit across
22	`Over.opEquivOpUnder`, the cone is rebuilt directly in `Under k`: the invariant
23	**subalgebra** `A^G` is already a `k`-algebra, so it is an object of `Under k` on the nose,
24	and the limit proof is the `CommRingCat` one with `(Under.forget k).map_injective` inserted
25	before each `hom_ext`. No transport, no `eqToHom`, no defeq wall.
26	
27	## Main results
28	
29	* `actionDiagramUnder` — the action as a diagram in `Under k`. Well-defined exactly because
30	  the action fixes the base: that is `[SMulCommClass G k A]`, and the proof is
31	  `algebraMap r = r • 1` followed by `smul_comm`.
32	* `fixedUnder` — `A^G` as an object of `Under k`, i.e. as a `k`-algebra.
33	* `fixedConeUnderIsLimit` — **the identification over the base**: the cone with vertex `A^G`
34	  is a limit cone in `Under k`.
35	* `hasLimit_actionDiagramUnder`, `fixedCoconeUnderIsColimitOp`,
36	  `hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op` — the `HasLimit` form and the dual, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`,
37	  which is the variance and the category of `SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra`.
38	* `hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op_symTensorPow` — the whole stack at Milne's ring: the
39	  `S_n`-action on `A^{⊗ n}` from `SymPowTensorAction`, quotiented over `k`.
40	* `hasColimit_singleObj_of_op` / `invEquivalence_comp_op_map` — the **index-category** step,
41	  which an earlier draft of this file wrongly treated as absent: `Functor.op` gives a diagram
42	  over `(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ`, not over `SingleObj G`, and the transport is `Groupoid.invEquivalence`
43	  with the reindexing being `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` on the nose.
44	
45	## What the hypothesis `[SMulCommClass G k A]` is, and why it is not a weakening
46	
47	`SymPowInvariants` assumed nothing beyond a `MulSemiringAction`. Over a base one must assume
48	the action is `k`-linear, otherwise the action maps are not morphisms of `Under k` and the
49	diagram does not exist. `SMulCommClass G k A` says exactly `g • (r • a) = r • (g • a)`, and
50	for Milne's case it holds: `permAlgHom` is an `R`-*algebra* hom by construction, so `R`-linear
51	by `map_smul`. That instance is supplied below (`permSMulCommClass`) rather than assumed.
52	
53	## Scope
54	
55	This closes the *category* item only. Still open, and untouched here:
56	
57	* **the gluing** — `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` in `Over (Spec k̄)` for the proper curve.
58	  `SymPowColimit.lean` §6 has the availability table; the affine charts now have a carrier
59	  over the base, which is what a `Scheme.GlueData` comparison on overlaps would need, but no
60	  glue data is built here.
61	* Consequently `AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are **unchanged**, and
62	  `albanese_universal_property` still reports `sorryAx`. Nothing below is a statement about
63	  `Sym^g C` for a curve.
64	
65	Two honest notes on consumption, since this lane has twice recorded claiming a gap closed
66	without a consumer (inbox `I-0571`, `I-0637`).
67	
68	**First**, no declaration in `SymPowColimit.lean` has been *rewritten* to consume
69	`hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op`; `grep` finds zero consumers of the names below. What
70	changed is that the obstruction is no longer a category mismatch.
71	
72	**Second — and this is a correction to a claim an earlier draft of this header made.** "Same
73	category, same variance" is not by itself enough, because the *index* category differs too:
74	`Functor.op` produces a diagram indexed by `(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ`, while
75	`SymPowColimit.permDiagram` is indexed by `SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))`. §5 closes that
76	third gap with `hasColimit_singleObj_of_op`, transporting along `Groupoid.invEquivalence`, and
77	records that the reindexing is exactly the `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` convention already carried twice
78	elsewhere in this cone. So the residual obstruction is mechanical (align `permAut` on
79	`(Under k)ᵒᵖ` with the reindexed diagram), not structural — but it is nonzero, and calling
80	this file's statements "directly consumable" would be the overclaim to avoid.
81	
82	## References
83	
84	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94. Consumers: this file's carrier is
85	the affine chart of `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §5.
86	-/
87	
88	set_option autoImplicit false
89	
90	universe u
91	
92	open CategoryTheory Limits
93	
94	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
95	
96	section UnderInvariants
97	
98	variable (k : CommRingCat.{u}) (G : Type u) [Group G] (A : Type u)
99	    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [MulSemiringAction G A] [SMulCommClass G k A]
100	
101	/-! ## §1. The action as a diagram over the base
102	
103	The only new content relative to `SymPowInvariants.actionDiagram` is the triangle: each
104	action map must commute with the structure morphism `k ⟶ A`. That is where
105	`[SMulCommClass G k A]` is spent, and it is spent once. -/
106	
107	/-- **A `k`-linear ring action, as a one-object diagram in `Under k`.**
108	
109	Same construction as `SymPowInvariants.actionDiagram`, but in the over-category: the
110	structure-map triangle holds because `algebraMap r = r • 1` and the action commutes with
111	scalars. -/
112	noncomputable def actionDiagramUnder : SingleObj G ⥤ Under k :=
113	  SingleObj.functor (M := G) (X := Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
114	    { toFun := fun g => Under.homMk (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A g))
115	          (by
116	            apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
117	            ext r
118	            change g • (algebraMap k A r) = algebraMap k A r
119	            rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, smul_comm, smul_one])
120	      map_one' := by
121	        apply (Under.forget k).map_injective
122	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
123	        ext (x : A)
124	        change (1 : G) • x = x
125	        rw [one_smul]
126	      map_mul' := by
127	        intro g h
128	        apply (Under.forget k).map_injective
129	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
130	        ext (x : A)
131	        change (g * h) • x = g • h • x
132	        rw [mul_smul] }
133	
134	/-- **`A^G` as a `k`-algebra**, i.e. as an object of `Under k`. Mathlib's
135	`FixedPoints.subalgebra` already *is* a `k`-subalgebra — this is only its packaging as an
136	`Under k` object, and it is why no transport across `Over.opEquivOpUnder` is needed. -/
137	noncomputable def fixedUnder : Under k :=
138	  Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (R := k) (S := FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G)
139	    (algebraMap k (FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G)))
140	
141	/-! ## §2. The invariants are the limit, over the base
142	
143	The proof is `SymPowInvariants.fixedConeIsLimit` with one insertion: a morphism of `Under k`
144	is determined by its underlying ring map, so each `hom_ext` is preceded by
145	`(Under.forget k).map_injective`. The cone condition and the lift are unchanged — an element
146	of the vertex lands in the invariants *because* the cone condition says its image is fixed. -/
147	
148	/-- **The cone over the action with vertex `A^G`, over the base.** -/
149	noncomputable def fixedConeUnder : Cone (actionDiagramUnder k G A) where
150	  pt := fixedUnder k G A
151	  π :=
152	    { app := fun _ => Under.homMk
153	        (CommRingCat.ofHom (R := FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G) (S := A)
154	          (FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G).subtype) (by
155	          apply CommRingCat.hom_ext; ext r; rfl)
156	      naturality := by
157	        intro X Y f
158	        apply (Under.forget k).map_injective
159	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
160	        ext (x : FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G)
161	        change ((x : A)) = (f : G) • (x : A)
162	        exact (x.2 _).symm }
163	
164	/-- **The identification over the base: `A^G` IS the limit in `Under k`.**
165	
166	This is the statement `SymPowInvariants` §4's third item asked for — same category as
167	`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra`, so a consumer there could take it, which nothing
168	could do with the `CommRingCat` version.
169	
170	The `lift`'s triangle obligation is the only step with no counterpart in the base-free proof:
171	that the lift respects the structure map. It reduces to the cone leg's own triangle
172	(`(c.π.app _).w`) after `Subtype.ext`, so it costs one `congrArg`. -/
173	noncomputable def fixedConeUnderIsLimit : IsLimit (fixedConeUnder k G A) where
174	  lift c := Under.homMk (V := fixedUnder k G A)
175	    (CommRingCat.ofHom (R := c.pt.right) (S := FixedPoints.subalgebra k A G)
176	      { toFun := fun t => ⟨(c.π.app (SingleObj.star G)).right.hom t, by
177	          intro g
178	          have h := c.w (SingleObj.toEnd G g)
179	          exact congrArg (fun (f : c.pt ⟶ (actionDiagramUnder k G A).obj (SingleObj.star G)) =>
180	            f.right.hom t) h⟩
181	        map_one' := by ext; exact map_one _
182	        map_mul' := by intro x y; ext; exact map_mul _ _ _
183	        map_zero' := by ext; exact map_zero _
184	        map_add' := by intro x y; ext; exact map_add _ _ _ })
185	    (by
186	      apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
187	      ext r
188	      refine Subtype.ext ?_
189	      have h : (c.π.app (SingleObj.star G)).right.hom (c.pt.hom.hom r)
190	          = (algebraMap k A) r :=
191	        (congrArg (fun (f : k ⟶ CommRingCat.of A) => f.hom r)
192	          (c.π.app (SingleObj.star G)).w : _)
193	      exact h)
194	  fac c j := by
195	    obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
196	    apply (Under.forget k).map_injective
197	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
198	    ext t
199	    rfl
200	  uniq c m hm := by
201	    apply (Under.forget k).map_injective
202	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
203	    ext t
204	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
205	    have h := hm (SingleObj.star G)
206	    exact congrArg (fun (f : c.pt ⟶ (actionDiagramUnder k G A).obj (SingleObj.star G)) =>
207	      f.right.hom t) h
208	
209	/-- **The `HasLimit` form over the base.** -/
210	theorem hasLimit_actionDiagramUnder : HasLimit (actionDiagramUnder k G A) :=
211	  ⟨⟨⟨fixedConeUnder k G A, fixedConeUnderIsLimit k G A⟩⟩⟩
212	
213	/-! ## §3. Dualised into `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` — the consumer's category and variance
214	
215	A quotient is a colimit, and `SymPowColimit`'s affine statement lives in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`. Both
216	now match: this is the same mathematics as `SymPowInvariants.fixedCoconeIsColimitOp`, in the
217	category that file could not reach. -/
218	
219	/-- **The affine quotient over the base, as a colimit in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`.**
220	
221	Geometrically: `Spec_k (A^G)` is the quotient of `Spec_k A` by `G`, as a `k`-scheme. This is
222	the statement in the category and variance of
223	`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra`. -/
224	noncomputable def fixedCoconeUnderIsColimitOp :
225	    IsColimit (fixedConeUnder k G A).op :=
226	  (fixedConeUnderIsLimit k G A).op
227	
228	/-- **The `HasColimit` form in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`**, with the colimit a named object. -/
229	theorem hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op : HasColimit (actionDiagramUnder k G A).op :=
230	  ⟨⟨⟨(fixedConeUnder k G A).op, fixedCoconeUnderIsColimitOp k G A⟩⟩⟩
231	
232	end UnderInvariants
233	
234	/-! ## §4. The whole stack at Milne's ring
235	
236	Everything above is for an arbitrary `k`-linear action. Instantiating at
237	`G := S_n`, `A := A^{⊗ n}` with the action of `Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` gives
238	Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1's affine half **over the base**, with the carrier named:
239	`Spec_k ((A^{⊗ n})^{S_n})` is the quotient of `(Spec_k A)^n` by the permutation action.
240	
241	The two hypotheses the instantiation needs — a `MulSemiringAction` and an `SMulCommClass` —
242	are both supplied there, not assumed: `permMulSemiringAction` and `permSMulCommClass`. As in
243	`SymPowTensorAction` §4, `Fin n` and `Type 0` are forced by `Under k`'s universe wanting the
244	group in the same universe as the ring. -/
245	
246	open PiTensorProduct TensorProduct
247	
248	variable (k : CommRingCat.{0}) (A : Type) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (n : ℕ)
249	
250	/-- **Milne's affine carrier is a quotient over the base** — the whole stack at his ring.
251	
252	`(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`, as a `k`-algebra, is the limit of the `S_n`-action on `A^{⊗ n}` in
253	`Under k`; dually `Spec_k` of it is the quotient of `(Spec_k A)^n`. This is the affine half of
254	Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 in the category and variance
255	`SymPowColimit.symPowData_affineAlgebra` uses.
256	
257	Still **not** `Sym^n C` for a proper curve: that is the gluing, and no glue data is built
258	here. See this file's scope section. -/
259	theorem hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op_symTensorPow :
260	    letI := permMulSemiringAction (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
261	    letI := permSMulCommClass (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
262	    HasColimit (actionDiagramUnder k (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (⨂[(k : Type)] _ : Fin n, A)).op :=
263	  letI := permMulSemiringAction (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
264	  letI := permSMulCommClass (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
265	  hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op _ _ _
266	
267	/-- **The limit form of the same statement**: `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}` is the limit of the
268	`S_n`-action over `k`. -/
269	theorem hasLimit_actionDiagramUnder_symTensorPow :
270	    letI := permMulSemiringAction (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
271	    letI := permSMulCommClass (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
272	    HasLimit (actionDiagramUnder k (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (⨂[(k : Type)] _ : Fin n, A)) :=
273	  letI := permMulSemiringAction (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
274	  letI := permSMulCommClass (k : Type) (ι := Fin n) A
275	  hasLimit_actionDiagramUnder _ _ _
276	
277	/-! ## §5. The index category is `(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ`, not `SingleObj G` — and that gap is real
278	
279	A trap caught while checking whether §3's colimit statement can actually be *consumed*, and
280	worth a lemma rather than a remark. `Functor.op` sends `F : SingleObj G ⥤ C` to
281	`F.op : (SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ`, so `hasColimit_actionDiagramUnder_op` is a statement about a
282	diagram indexed by **`(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ`**. But `SymPowColimit.permDiagram` — what
283	`symPowData_of_hasColimit` consumes — is indexed by `SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))` itself.
284	Those are different index categories, so "same category, same variance" was two thirds of the
285	story and the shape was the missing third.
286	
287	They are *equivalent*, because a groupoid is equivalent to its opposite via `g ↦ g⁻¹`
288	(`Groupoid.invEquivalence`), and `hasColimit_singleObj_of_op` below transports the colimit
289	along it. Note what the transported diagram is: precomposition with that equivalence
290	reindexes the action by inversion, which is `rfl`-checked in
291	`invEquivalence_comp_op_map` — the *same* `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` bookkeeping that
292	`SymPowTensorAction.permMulSemiringAction` and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` each carry, appearing a
293	third time. Three independent occurrences of one inversion is a sign the convention is
294	coherent, not that something is off.
295	
296	What this does **not** do: it does not rewrite `symPowData_affineAlgebra` to consume the
297	named carrier. The obstruction to that is now purely mechanical (align `permAut` on
298	`(Under k)ᵒᵖ` with the reindexed action diagram), where before it was a category mismatch. -/
299	
300	/-- **Transport across the groupoid inverse equivalence.** A colimit of `F.op` — indexed by
301	`(SingleObj G)ᵒᵖ` — yields a colimit of a diagram indexed by `SingleObj G`, namely `F.op`
302	reindexed by inversion. This is what makes §3's statement usable by a consumer written
303	against `SingleObj G`. -/
304	theorem hasColimit_singleObj_of_op {G : Type u} [Group G] {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C]
305	    (F : SingleObj G ⥤ C) [HasColimit F.op] :
306	    HasColimit ((Groupoid.invEquivalence (SingleObj G)).functor ⋙ F.op) :=
307	  inferInstance
308	
309	/-- **The reindexing is exactly inversion**, on the nose. So the transported diagram of
310	`hasColimit_singleObj_of_op` is the original action read backwards — the third appearance of
311	the `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` convention in this cone. -/
312	theorem invEquivalence_comp_op_map {G : Type u} [Group G] {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C]
313	    (F : SingleObj G ⥤ C) (g : G) :
314	    ((Groupoid.invEquivalence (SingleObj G)).functor ⋙ F.op).map (SingleObj.toEnd G g)
315	      = (F.map (SingleObj.toEnd G g⁻¹)).op := rfl
316	
317	end AlgebraicGeometry
318	
319

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.SymPowInvariants
8	
9	/-!
10	# Milne's `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`: the symmetric group acting on a tensor power of a ring
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean` proved that the invariant subring `A^G` **is** the limit of
13	a group action in `CommRingCat`, hence a colimit — a quotient — in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`. Its §4
14	then listed three things that identification still lacked, and the second was this:
15	
16	> The specialisation to Milne's actual ring. `G := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` acting on the
17	> `n`-fold tensor power `A^{⊗ n}` is the case Milne uses; the `S_n`-action on a tensor
18	> power of a commutative *ring* is not built here (mathlib's symmetric API is for
19	> modules — `PiTensorProduct.reindex` is a *linear* equiv).
20	
21	This file supplies it. Mathlib has the commutative ring and `R`-algebra structure on
22	`⨂[R] i, A i` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PiTensorProduct.lean`) and it has factor permutation as
23	a *linear* equivalence, but nothing upgrades the permutation to a ring or algebra map, so
24	`MulSemiringAction (Equiv.Perm ι) (⨂[R] _ : ι, A)` does not synthesize. Without that
25	instance `FixedPoints.subring`/`subalgebra` cannot even be *stated* at the tensor power, so
26	Milne's formula was not expressible in the tree.
27	
28	## Main results
29	
30	* `PiTensorProduct.permAlgHom` — factor permutation as an `R`-**algebra** homomorphism of
31	  `⨂[R] _ : ι, A`, built from `liftAlgHom` on the reindexed `tprod`.
32	* `PiTensorProduct.permAlgHom_comp` — the composition law, and note its **variance**:
33	  `permAlgHom σ ∘ permAlgHom τ = permAlgHom (τ * σ)`, an *anti*-homomorphism.
34	* `PiTensorProduct.permAlgEquiv` — hence the algebra automorphism.
35	* `PiTensorProduct.permMulSemiringAction` — the left `S_n`-action, taking `σ` to
36	  `permAlgHom σ⁻¹`. The inverse is forced by the previous item, exactly as
37	  `SymPowColimit.permEnd` needs `σ⁻¹` on the geometric side.
38	* `PiTensorProduct.permSMulCommClass` — the action commutes with scalars (one `map_smul`).
39	  `FixedPoints.subalgebra` needs this *in addition to* the `MulSemiringAction`, and mathlib
40	  supplies neither at a tensor power; it is also what makes the action a diagram over the
41	  base ring (`Albanese/SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean`).
42	* `symTensorPowSubalgebra R A` — **Milne's `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`**, as an `R`-subalgebra, with
43	  `mem_symTensorPowSubalgebra_iff` and `symTensorPowSubalgebra_toSubring`. The universal
44	  property is *not* restated here as an algebra statement; it arrives in categorical form
45	  through the next item, which is where the limit/colimit property is proved.
46	* `hasLimit_actionDiagram_symTensorPow` / `hasColimit_actionDiagram_op_symTensorPow` — the
47	  same fact as a limit in `CommRingCat` and a colimit in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, obtained by
48	  instantiating `SymPowInvariants`' general theorems at this action. This is the first
49	  place in the tree where Milne's affine carrier appears as a named object with a proved
50	  quotient property.
51	
52	## Characteristic-free, and no finiteness on the ring
53	
54	Nothing here averages over the group, so no `n!` is inverted and the statements hold in
55	every characteristic — which matters, since `Sym^g C` is wanted over an arbitrary
56	algebraically closed `k̄` and `g!` may vanish there. `ι` is arbitrary (not even finite) for
57	the action itself; `Fin n` enters only when specialising to Milne's `n`-fold power.
58	
59	## Scope — what this is not
60	
61	This is **affine commutative algebra**. It does not construct `Sym^n C` for a curve, and it
62	does not close `SymPowInvariants` §4's other two items:
63	
64	* the curve case still needs `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` in `Over (Spec k̄)`, i.e. the
65	  gluing (`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6);
66	* the **category** caveat stands. `SymPowColimit`'s affine inhabitation statement
67	  `symPowData_affineAlgebra` lives in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`; everything here, like
68	  `SymPowInvariants`, lives in `CommRingCat`/`CommRingCatᵒᵖ` with no base ring in the
69	  *category*, even though the ring statements are `R`-algebra statements. Bridging those
70	  two remains open, so no declaration in `SymPowColimit.lean` consumes anything below.
71	
72	Read this file, then, as: *Milne's affine carrier is now nameable and its universal
73	property is proved*, not as *Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 is formalised*.
74	
75	## References
76	
77	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94 (the symmetric power as
78	`Spec (A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}` glued over an affine cover). Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, §II.7.

93	/-! ## §1. Factor permutation as an algebra homomorphism
94	
95	The multilinear map `x ↦ tprod R (x ∘ e)` is unital and multiplicative on the nose, since
96	`(x * y) ∘ e = (x ∘ e) * (y ∘ e)` pointwise, so `liftAlgHom` applies with no side
97	conditions to discharge beyond those two equations. -/
98	
99	/-- **Factor permutation, as an `R`-algebra endomorphism of the tensor power.**
100	
101	`permAlgHom R A e` sends `a_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a_n` to the tuple reindexed along `e`:
102	`tprod x ↦ tprod (x ∘ e)`. Mathlib has this as a linear equivalence only
103	(`PiTensorProduct.reindex`); the algebra structure is what the invariant *subring* needs. -/
104	noncomputable def permAlgHom (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
105	    (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) →ₐ[R] (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) :=
106	  liftAlgHom ((tprod R (s := fun _ : ι => A)).domDomCongr e)
107	    (by
108	      simp only [MultilinearMap.domDomCongr_apply]
109	      exact (one_def (R := R) (A := fun _ : ι => A)).symm)
110	    (by
111	      intro x y
112	      simp only [MultilinearMap.domDomCongr_apply]
113	      rw [show (fun i => (x * y) (e i)) = (fun i => x (e i)) * (fun i => y (e i)) from rfl,
114	        tprod_mul_tprod])
115	
116	@[simp]
117	theorem permAlgHom_tprod (e : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : ι → A) :
118	    permAlgHom R A e (tprod R x) = tprod R (fun i => x (e i)) := by
119	  simp [permAlgHom]
120	
121	variable [Finite ι]
122	
123	/-- **The composition law, with its variance.** Reindexing along `e` then along `d`
124	reindexes along `e * d`… on the *tuples*, which is `d * e` read as permutations acting on
125	indices. Concretely `permAlgHom d ∘ permAlgHom e = permAlgHom (e * d)`: the assignment is an
126	*anti*-homomorphism, and that is why `permMulSemiringAction` below inserts an inverse.
127	
128	The same bookkeeping appears on the geometric side in `SymPowColimit.permEnd`, for the
129	mirror-image reason (mathlib's `End` multiplication is `f * g = g ≫ f`). -/
130	theorem permAlgHom_comp (d e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
131	    (permAlgHom R A d).comp (permAlgHom R A e) = permAlgHom R A (e * d) := by
132	  classical
133	  ext i a
134	  simp [Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]
135	
136	@[simp]
137	theorem permAlgHom_one : permAlgHom R A (1 : Equiv.Perm ι) = AlgHom.id R _ := by
138	  classical
139	  ext i a
140	  simp
141	
142	/-- **Factor permutation as an algebra automorphism.** Its inverse is the permutation
143	`e⁻¹`, by `permAlgHom_comp` and `permAlgHom_one`. -/
144	noncomputable def permAlgEquiv (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
145	    (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) ≃ₐ[R] (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) :=
146	  AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom (permAlgHom R A e) (permAlgHom R A e⁻¹)
147	    (by rw [permAlgHom_comp]; simp)
148	    (by rw [permAlgHom_comp]; simp)
149	
150	@[simp]
151	theorem permAlgEquiv_tprod (e : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : ι → A) :
152	    permAlgEquiv R A e (tprod R x) = tprod R (fun i => x (e i)) :=
153	  permAlgHom_tprod R A e x
154	
155	/-! ## §2. The action, with the inverse that makes it a left action
156	
157	`permAlgHom` is an anti-homomorphism (`permAlgHom_comp`), so `σ • x := permAlgHom σ x` would
158	be a *right* action. Taking `σ • x := permAlgHom σ⁻¹ x` fixes the variance, and gives the
159	`MulSemiringAction` that `FixedPoints.subring` consumes.
160	
161	This is the instance whose absence made Milne's formula unstateable: `FixedPoints.subring`
162	requires `MulSemiringAction G A`, and mathlib's `PiTensorProduct.reindex` — being only a
163	linear equivalence — cannot supply it. -/
164	
165	/-- **The `S_ι`-action on the tensor power, as a `MulSemiringAction`.**
166	
167	`σ • (a_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a_n) = a_{σ⁻¹ 1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a_{σ⁻¹ n}`. The inverse is what turns the
168	anti-homomorphism `permAlgHom` into a left action; see `permAlgHom_comp`.
169	
170	Deliberately **not** a global `instance`: the tensor power carries other group actions in
171	principle, and a global instance on `⨂[R] _ : ι, A` would fire during unrelated synthesis.
172	Consumers name it with `letI`, exactly as `SymPowInvariants` expects its
173	`MulSemiringAction` to be supplied. -/
174	@[implicit_reducible]
175	noncomputable def permMulSemiringAction :
176	    MulSemiringAction (Equiv.Perm ι) (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) where
177	  smul σ x := permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹ x
178	  one_smul x := by
179	    change permAlgHom R A (1 : Equiv.Perm ι)⁻¹ x = x
180	    rw [inv_one, permAlgHom_one]; rfl
181	  mul_smul σ τ x := by
182	    change permAlgHom R A (σ * τ)⁻¹ x = permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹ (permAlgHom R A τ⁻¹ x)
183	    have h := permAlgHom_comp R A (σ⁻¹) (τ⁻¹)
184	    rw [mul_inv_rev]
185	    exact (AlgHom.congr_fun h x).symm
186	  smul_zero σ := map_zero (permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹)
187	  smul_add σ x y := map_add (permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹) x y
188	  smul_one σ := map_one (permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹)
189	  smul_mul σ x y := map_mul (permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹) x y
190	
191	/-- **The action commutes with scalars.** Immediate from `permAlgHom` being an *algebra*
192	hom, hence `R`-linear — one `map_smul`.
193	
194	Needed because `FixedPoints.subalgebra` requires `[SMulCommClass G R B]` in addition to the
195	`MulSemiringAction`, and mathlib supplies neither at a tensor power. It is also the
196	hypothesis under which the action is a diagram in `Under R` rather than merely in
197	`CommRingCat`; see `Albanese/SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean`. -/
198	@[implicit_reducible]
199	noncomputable def permSMulCommClass :
200	    letI := permMulSemiringAction R (ι := ι) A
201	    SMulCommClass (Equiv.Perm ι) R (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) :=
202	  letI := permMulSemiringAction R (ι := ι) A
203	  ⟨fun σ r x => map_smul (permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹) r x⟩
204	
205	/-- The action, unfolded. Note `(ι := ι)`: `permMulSemiringAction`'s index type is
206	implicit and does not appear in its explicit arguments, so a bare
207	`letI := permMulSemiringAction R A` in a *statement* leaves `ι` a metavariable and the
208	`HSMul` instance search gets stuck. Every `letI` of this action below names `ι`. -/
209	theorem permSmul_def (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : ⨂[R] _ : ι, A) :
210	    letI := permMulSemiringAction R (ι := ι) A
211	    σ • x = permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹ x := rfl
212	
213	/-! ## §3. Milne's carrier `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`
214	
215	Two forms, and the reason for both. `symTensorPowSubalgebra` states invariance *directly*
216	(`∀ σ, permAlgHom σ x = x`) so that the type mentions no action instance: with the action a
217	`letI`-supplied `def` rather than a global instance, a subalgebra whose very type depended on
218	it would be painful at every use site. `symTensorPowSubalgebra_toSubring` then identifies it
219	with `FixedPoints.subring` for the `letI` action, which is what
220	`Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean` proves to be the limit.
221	
222	Note the direction bookkeeping in that identification: `σ • x = permAlgHom σ⁻¹ x`, and
223	quantifying over all `σ` makes the inverse invisible — invariance under all of `S_n` is the
224	same set either way. That is the only content of the proof, and it is worth having as a
225	lemma because it is exactly where a sign error would hide. -/
226	
227	/-- **Milne's `(A^{⊗ n})^{S_n}`, as an `R`-subalgebra.**
228	
229	An element is in it iff every factor permutation fixes it. Stated with `permAlgHom`
230	directly, so that the type does not mention `permMulSemiringAction` — see the §3 header for
231	why that matters. -/
232	noncomputable def symTensorPowSubalgebra : Subalgebra R (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) where
233	  carrier := {x | ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm ι, permAlgHom R A σ x = x}
234	  mul_mem' hx hy σ := by
235	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at *
236	    rw [map_mul, hx, hy]
237	  one_mem' σ := map_one _
238	  add_mem' hx hy σ := by
239	    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at *
240	    rw [map_add, hx, hy]
241	  zero_mem' σ := map_zero _
242	  algebraMap_mem' r σ := AlgHom.commutes _ r
243	
244	omit [Finite ι] in
245	@[simp]
246	theorem mem_symTensorPowSubalgebra_iff (x : ⨂[R] _ : ι, A) :
247	    x ∈ symTensorPowSubalgebra R A ↔ ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm ι, permAlgHom R A σ x = x := Iff.rfl
248	
249	/-- **The two descriptions agree**: the directly-stated invariants are the fixed points of
250	the `MulSemiringAction`. The inverse in `permSmul_def` washes out because the condition
251	quantifies over the whole group.
252	
253	This is the lemma that lets `Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean`'s general theorems — stated for
254	`FixedPoints.subring` — be read as statements about Milne's carrier. -/
255	theorem symTensorPowSubalgebra_toSubring :
256	    letI := permMulSemiringAction R (ι := ι) A
257	    (symTensorPowSubalgebra R A).toSubring
258	      = FixedPoints.subring (⨂[R] _ : ι, A) (Equiv.Perm ι) := by
259	  letI := permMulSemiringAction R (ι := ι) A
260	  ext x
261	  constructor
262	  · intro h g
263	    exact h g⁻¹
264	  · intro h σ
265	    have hx : permAlgHom R A σ⁻¹⁻¹ x = x := h σ⁻¹
266	    rwa [inv_inv] at hx
267	
268	omit [Finite ι] in
269	/-- **A tensor of a constant tuple is invariant** — the diagonal `a ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a` lies in
270	Milne's carrier, since permuting a constant tuple does nothing.
271	
272	Kept as a supply of elements: it exhibits the diagonal image of `A` inside the carrier, so
273	the invariants are not obviously just `algebraMap R`'s image. Note what this does **not**
274	prove — that the containment is *strict* for some `A`, which would need an element of
275	`⨂ A` shown outside the image of `R`, and no declaration here does that. So read it as a
276	witness that the carrier has describable elements, not as a non-vacuity theorem; contrast
277	`SymPowColimit.permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`, which is a genuine non-vacuity statement
278	because it refutes an equality. -/
279	theorem tprod_const_mem_symTensorPowSubalgebra (a : A) :
280	    tprod R (fun _ : ι => a) ∈ symTensorPowSubalgebra R A := by
281	  intro σ
282	  simp
283	
284	end Action

9	/-!
10	# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
11	
12	`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
13	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
14	needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
15	stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
16	quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
17	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
18	
19	That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
20	it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
21	
22	## What was actually going on
23	
24	`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
25	for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
26	a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
27	the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
28	`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
29	`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
30	`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
31	
32	So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
33	data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
34	generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
35	copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
36	being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
37	direction that should go.
38	
39	## Main results
40	
41	* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
42	  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
43	* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
44	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
45	  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
46	  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
47	* `permAction` — the `S_n`-action on a product, as the `MonoidHom` this file consumes, so the
48	  symmetric-power case can be fed in directly.
49	
50	## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
51	
52	The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
53	characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
54	`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
55	through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
56	
57	## Scope — what this does and does not give
58	
59	**Does**: the stable-cover input to a glue-data construction, for `S_n` acting on `C^n`, with
60	no Galois hypothesis and no characteristic hypothesis.
61	
62	**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open, and
63	`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged. Two further inputs a glue-data assembly needs
64	are also unaddressed here: that the affine chart quotients agree on overlaps (the cocycle
65	condition), and `OrbitsInAffineOpen` **for the curve** — which is where quasi-projectivity
66	would enter, and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin. So this closes one
67	of three, and the remaining two are named rather than estimated.
68	
69	Note also: nothing consumes this file yet. It is stated so the `S_n` case *can* consume it,
70	which is a different claim from having wired it in.
71	
72	## References
73	
74	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94. EGA II 4.5.4 for the
75	orbit-in-affine hypothesis. The original proof is
76	`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction.exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`
77	(`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean:193`), whose supporting lemmas
78	(`exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`, `mem_finset_inf`, `preimage_finset_inf`,
79	`basicOpen_finset_prod`) are imported and reused unchanged.
80	-/

92	variable {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {X : Scheme.{u}} (act : G →* Aut X)
93	
94	/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis for a bare action** (EGA II 4.5.4): every orbit is contained
95	in an affine open. This hypothesis is *essential*, not a convenience — without it the
96	quotient need only be an algebraic space (Hironaka; see `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s
97	module docstring). It holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
98	at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by hand. -/
99	def OrbitsInAffineOpen : Prop :=
100	  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ g : G, (act g).hom.base x ∈ U.1
101	
102	/-- A `G`-stable open of `X`. -/
103	def IsStableOpen (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
104	  ∀ g : G, (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U

106	omit [Finite G] in
107	/-- The identity acts as the identity. This and `act_mul_hom` are the *only* structural facts
108	the main theorem uses about the action — both are `map_one`/`map_mul` of the `MonoidHom`,

133	theorem exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits (h : OrbitsInAffineOpen act) (x : X) :

161	    rw [ht, Scheme.basicOpen_res, ← Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
162	  -- the `g = 1` translate is `D(s)` itself
163	  have hP1 : (act (1 : G)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s = X.basicOpen s := by
164	    rw [act_one_hom act]; rfl
165	  -- `D(N) = ⋂_g (act g)⁻¹ D(s)`
166	  have hbo_N : X.basicOpen N = Finset.univ.inf fun g : G => (act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
167	    rw [hN, basicOpen_finset_prod ⟨1, Finset.mem_univ 1⟩,
168	      Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hbo_t g]
169	    refine le_antisymm
170	      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)).trans inf_le_right)
171	      (Finset.le_inf fun g _ => le_inf (le_trans ?_ hs_le)
172	        (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ g)))
173	    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
174	  -- `D(N) ⊆ D(s)` (the `g = 1` factor)
175	  have hNs : X.basicOpen N ≤ X.basicOpen s := by
176	    rw [hbo_N]
177	    exact le_of_le_of_eq (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ 1)) hP1
178	  refine ⟨X.basicOpen N, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
179	  · -- affineness: `D(N)` is a basic open of the affine `D(s)`
180	    have heq : X.basicOpen (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hs_le).op N) = X.basicOpen N := by
181	      rw [Scheme.basicOpen_res]
182	      exact inf_eq_right.mpr hNs
183	    rw [← heq]
184	    exact (U.2.basicOpen s).basicOpen _
185	  · -- membership: prime avoidance put the whole orbit in `D(s)`
186	    rw [hbo_N, mem_finset_inf]
187	    intro g _
188	    change (act g).hom.base x ∈ X.basicOpen s
189	    exact hs_mem g
190	  · -- stability, at the level of opens: preimage functoriality plus reindexing
191	    intro tau
192	    rw [hbo_N, preimage_finset_inf]
193	    have hPt : ∀ g : G, (act tau).hom ⁻¹ᵁ ((act g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
194	        = (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s := by
195	      intro g
196	      rw [act_mul_hom act]; rfl
197	    rw [Finset.inf_congr rfl fun g _ => hPt g]
198	    refine le_antisymm (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_) (Finset.le_inf fun d _ => ?_)
199	    · have hh := Finset.inf_le (s := Finset.univ)
200	        (f := fun g : G => (act (g * tau)).hom ⁻¹ᵁ X.basicOpen s)
201	        (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau⁻¹))
202	      rwa [inv_mul_cancel_right] at hh
203	    · exact Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ (d * tau))

83	variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]

85	/-! ## §1. The permutation action as a diagram
86	
87	`MonObj.permAut` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`) gives the factor-permuting endomorphism
88	of `C^n`. Bundling it as a monoid homomorphism into `End (C^n)` turns the `S_n`-action
89	into a functor out of `SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))`, which is the shape mathlib's
90	colimit API consumes.
91	
92	One convention point worth stating, since it is the only place a sign can go wrong:
93	composition in `End X` is `f * g = g ≫ f`, so a *homomorphism* out of `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`
94	must use `σ ↦ permAut C σ⁻¹`. With that inverse the multiplicativity is `rfl` after
95	projecting; without it one gets an anti-homomorphism. -/
96	
97	/-- **The `S_n`-action on `C^n`, as a monoid homomorphism into `End (C^n)`.**
98	
99	Sends `σ` to `permAut C σ⁻¹`. The inverse is forced by mathlib's `End` convention
100	(`f * g = g ≫ f`); see the section note. -/
101	noncomputable def permEnd (C : K) (n : ℕ) :
102	    Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* End (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) where
103	  toFun σ := MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹
104	  map_one' := by
105	    apply Pi.hom_ext; intro i
106	    rw [MonObj.permAut_π]; simp
107	  map_mul' σ τ := by
108	    apply Pi.hom_ext; intro i
109	    change MonObj.permAut C (σ * τ)⁻¹ ≫ _ = (MonObj.permAut C τ⁻¹ ≫ MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹) ≫ _
110	    rw [MonObj.permAut_π, Category.assoc, MonObj.permAut_π, MonObj.permAut_π]
111	    rfl
112	
113	/-- **The permutation-action diagram.** The one-object diagram in `K` whose single value
114	is `C^n` and whose endomorphisms are the factor permutations. A colimit of it is the
115	quotient `C^n / S_n`. -/
116	noncomputable def permDiagram (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) ⥤ K :=
117	  SingleObj.functor (permEnd C n)
118	
119	variable (C : K) (n : ℕ)
120	
121	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
122	/-- The diagram's value at the unique object is `C^n`. -/
123	theorem permDiagram_obj (j : SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) :
124	    (permDiagram C n).obj j = ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) := rfl
125	
126	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
127	/-- **The action, expressed as a diagram map.** `permAut C σ` is the diagram's map at
128	`σ⁻¹`; the double inverse is the `End`-convention bookkeeping of `permEnd`. This is the
129	bridge every proof below crosses. -/
130	theorem permAut_eq_map (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
131	    MonObj.permAut C σ = (permDiagram C n).map (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹) := by
132	  change MonObj.permAut C σ = MonObj.permAut C σ⁻¹⁻¹
133	  rw [inv_inv]
134	
135	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
136	/-- **Every cocone leg is symmetric.** This is the cocone condition `Cocone.w` read
137	through `permAut_eq_map`, and it is the reason the symmetry hypothesis of `SymPowData`
138	costs nothing on the colimit side. -/
139	theorem cocone_app_perm (c : Cocone (permDiagram C n)) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
140	    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _) = c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _) := by
141	  rw [permAut_eq_map C n σ]
142	  exact c.w (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹)
143	
144	/-- **A symmetric morphism out of `C^n` is a cocone.** The converse packaging of
145	`cocone_app_perm`: `S_n`-invariance of `h` is exactly the cocone condition. -/
146	noncomputable def symCocone {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T)
147	    (hsym : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) :
148	    Cocone (permDiagram C n) where
149	  pt := T
150	  ι :=
151	    { app := fun _ => h
152	      naturality := by
153	        intro X Y f
154	        change MonObj.permAut C (f : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))⁻¹ ≫ h = h ≫ 𝟙 T
155	        rw [Category.comp_id]
156	        exact hsym _ }
157	
158	/-! ## §2. A colimit of the action is a `SymPowData`, with symmetry for free
159	
160	This is the forward half of the identification. Note which part is doing the work: the
161	universal property of `SymPowData` is `colimit.desc` plus `colimit.hom_ext`, and the
162	symmetry hypothesis `hproj` — the half that ruled out the trivial witness and had only
163	an `n = 1` witness before — is `colimit.w`. Nothing is assumed about `n`. -/
164	
165	section OfColimit
166	
167	variable [HasColimit (permDiagram C n)]
168	
169	/-- **The symmetric power from a colimit of the permutation action.**
170	
171	`carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)`, `proj := colimit.ι`, and the universal property is
172	`colimit.desc` — a symmetric `h` is a cocone by `symCocone`, and uniqueness is
173	`colimit.hom_ext` on the one-object index category. -/
174	noncomputable def symPowOfColimit : SymPowData C n where
175	  carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)
176	  proj := colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
177	  desc := fun {T} h hsym => by
178	    have hd : colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
179	        ≫ colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym) = h :=
180	      colimit.ι_desc (symCocone C n h hsym) (SingleObj.star _)
181	    refine ⟨colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym), hd, ?_⟩
182	    intro u hu
183	    exact colimit.hom_ext fun j => by
184	      obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
185	      exact hu.trans hd.symm
186	
187	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
188	@[simp]
189	theorem symPowOfColimit_carrier :
190	    (symPowOfColimit C n).carrier = colimit (permDiagram C n) := rfl
191	
192	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
193	@[simp]
194	theorem symPowOfColimit_proj :
195	    (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) := rfl
196	
197	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
198	/-- **The symmetry hypothesis, for free.** The projection of `symPowOfColimit` is
199	`S_n`-symmetric because that is the cocone condition `colimit.w`.
200	
201	This is the declaration that changes the interface's status: `SymPowInterface.lean` needs
202	the *pair* `(D, hproj)`, and here `hproj` comes with the object at no cost and at every
203	`n`. -/
204	theorem symPowOfColimit_proj_perm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
205	    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = (symPowOfColimit C n).proj := by
206	  have h := colimit.w (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹)
207	  change MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) = _
208	  rw [permAut_eq_map C n σ]
209	  exact h
210	
211	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
212	/-- **The pair, packaged.** Existence of the object the Albanese theorems quantify over,
213	in the form a call site consumes: a `SymPowData` *together with* its symmetry. -/
214	theorem symPowData_of_hasColimit :
215	    ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
216	      MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
217	  ⟨symPowOfColimit C n, symPowOfColimit_proj_perm C n⟩
218	
219	end OfColimit
220	
221	/-! ## §3. Conversely: the pair *is* a colimit
222	
223	The other half of the identification, and the one that makes the reduction lossless. Any
224	`SymPowData` whose projection is symmetric exhibits its carrier as a colimit of
225	`permDiagram C n`.
226	
227	Consequence worth stating explicitly, because it is what rules out having traded the
228	problem for a harder one: nobody can supply the pair `(D, hproj)` *without* supplying this
229	colimit. So `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` is not a sufficient condition that might be
230	stronger than needed — it is equivalent to the thing the Albanese argument consumes. -/
231	
232	section ToColimit
233	
234	/-- The cocone attached to a `SymPowData` with symmetric projection. -/
235	noncomputable def SymPowData.cocone (D : SymPowData C n)
236	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj) :
237	    Cocone (permDiagram C n) where
238	  pt := D.carrier

10	# Naming the affine symmetric-power carrier: the quotient is `Spec` of the invariants
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` reduced the symmetric-power obligation to one instance,
13	`HasColimit (permDiagram C n)`, and proved that the affine-algebra case is *inhabited*
14	at every `n`. But it flagged, three times and deliberately, that the resulting object
15	was **not identified**:
16	
17	> `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` is the *reason to expect* it … but it is a statement about
18	> `SingleObj G ⥤ Type` and mentions neither `CommRingCat` nor `Spec`. **The carrier is not
19	> named in Lean.**
20	
21	The *naming* half of that gap is answered here: the colimit of a group action on a ring,
22	taken in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, is `A^G`. It becomes Milne's `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` only once `A` is
23	the `n`-fold tensor power carrying the `S_n`-action — which is **not** supplied below (see
24	the scope section). So read this as *the carrier of a ring-action quotient is now a named
25	object with a proved universal property*, not as *`SymPowColimit`'s flagged obligation is
26	discharged*: that obligation also wants the tensor power, the `S_n`-action on it, and a
27	category match, and all three are still open.
28	
29	## Why naming the carrier is real content, not bookkeeping
30	
31	The inhabitation statement `symPowData_affineAlgebra` comes from mathlib's colimits and
32	says only *some* object has the universal property. Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 says what
33	it **is**, and the difference is not cosmetic: the gluing step — the leg's remaining work
34	— has to compare the quotients of two overlapping charts. A comparison needs a formula for
35	each side. An abstract `colimit (permDiagram …)` supports no such comparison; `A^G` does,
36	because restriction of invariants along `A → A_b` is a ring map one can write down.
37	
38	So this file supplies a prerequisite for gluing rather than restating what was known. Note
39	the modest claim: it is *a* prerequisite, and no declaration in the tree consumes it yet
40	(grep for `fixedConeIsLimit` outside this file returns nothing). Calling it "what the next
41	step consumes" would be premature until the category caveat below is closed.
42	
43	## Main results
44	
45	* `actionDiagram G A` — the one-object diagram in `CommRingCat` of a `MulSemiringAction`.
46	  This is `permDiagram`'s algebraic counterpart: same index category `SingleObj G`.
47	* `fixedCone` / `fixedConeIsLimit` — **the identification, as a limit in `CommRingCat`**:
48	  the cone over `actionDiagram` with vertex the fixed subring `A^G` (mathlib's
49	  `FixedPoints.subring`) is a limit cone. Nothing is assumed about `G` — not even
50	  finiteness — because the universal property of the invariants needs none.
51	* `fixedCoconeIsColimitOp` — the same fact **dualised**: in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, `A^G` is a
52	  *colimit* of the action, which is the variance a quotient has.
53	* `hasColimit_actionDiagram_op` — hence the `HasColimit` statement for the opposite
54	  diagram, with the carrier now named.
55	
56	**One category caveat, and it is load-bearing — a fresh-context review caught an earlier
57	draft of this header asserting otherwise.** `SymPowColimit`'s affine statement
58	(`symPowData_affineAlgebra`) lives in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`, the opposite of `k`-algebras; this file
59	lives in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, with no base ring. **Those are different categories**, and no
60	declaration here bridges them (`Over.opEquivOpUnder` and `AffineScheme.equivCommRingCat`
61	exist in mathlib but are not used below). So nothing in `SymPowColimit.lean` can currently
62	*consume* `hasColimit_actionDiagram_op`: this is a parallel identification of the same
63	mathematics over a different base, not a plugged-in input. Supplying the bridge — or
64	restating the below over `Under k` — is unfinished work.
65	
66	## Scope — read this before quoting it
67	
68	What is proved is the **affine, algebraic** identification: a limit in `CommRingCat` and
69	its dual in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`. Two things are deliberately *not* claimed:

73	  universal property transfers into `Scheme` only against *affine* test objects.

75	  ring. Specialising `G := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` and `A := A^{⊗ n}` is what makes it Milne's
76	  statement; that specialisation needs the `S_n`-action on the tensor power, which mathlib
77	  has for modules and which is not built here.
78	
79	So: the carrier of the affine quotient is now a named object with a written-down universal
80	property, which is what the next step consumes. It is not the symmetric power of a curve.
81	
82	## References

85	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §5; the interface is `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`.
